words.gloss: accomplishment (of remedy) of the mishaps of vomiting and purging

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम वमन और विरेचन की व्यापत्सिद्धि की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the accomplishment (siddhi) in the mishaps of vomiting and purging.
notes: siddhi in the chapter title is rendered literally as 'accomplishment'; the compound can also be read 'the successful treatment of mishaps in vomiting and purging'. Chapter-opening formula.

hindi: जो अत्यन्त भूखा हो, मृदु कोष्ठ वाला हो, जिसमें श्लेष्मा थोड़ा हो, जिसे वमन कराना कठिन हो, या जो दुर्बल हो, अथवा औषध मात्रा में कम, अति तीक्ष्ण, अति शीत हो, या अजीर्ण में पिया गया हो, तो पिया हुआ वमन नीचे की ओर जाता है।
english: In one who is very hungry, soft in the bowel, with little phlegm, hard to make vomit, or weak; or if the vomiting-medicine is of deficient dose, very sharp, very cold, or is drunk in indigestion, the vomiting-medicine drunk goes downward.

text_flags.why: possible: b for v; 'hard to make vomit' fits the sense and the list of instrumentals

notes: Instrumentals are rendered 'in one who'. The reading of hīnamātra...ajīrṇe as a list of conditions of the medicine and the patient follows the plainest sense; ajīrṇe could also be 'in one with indigestion'.

hindi: वहाँ इच्छित फल की प्राप्ति नहीं होती और मल उभर आता है।
english: In that case the desired result is not obtained, and the waste matter (mala) is stirred up.

words.gloss: by suitable (ones), by those in proper combination
with regard to dose, time and so on

hindi: उसे फिर शीघ्र उपयुक्त साधनों से स्नेहयुक्त करके मात्रा, काल आदि का ध्यान रखते हुए वमन कराए।
english: Having quickly made him unctuous again with suitable means, one should make him vomit, with regard to dose, time and so on.
notes: yaugikaiḥ is taken as 'by suitable (means)'; the noun to be supplied is not stated.

hindi: और पहले हुई भूल को स्मरण करते हुए व्यापद् के कारणों से बचे।
english: And, remembering the earlier error, one should avoid the causes of mishap.

words.gloss: very hot, sharp, salty, or of great dose

hindi: अजीर्ण वाले और कफ वाले पुरुष में अति उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, लवण अथवा मात्रा में बहुत बड़ा विरेचन, या कोई अन्य औषध, ऊपर की ओर प्रवृत्त होता है।
english: In one with indigestion or one having phlegm, a purgative that is very hot, sharp, salty, or of great dose, or another medicine, goes upward.

text_flags.why: possible: garbled; 'greatness of dose' fits the list

notes: The printed spelling pravarttate (double t) is the edition's usual spelling of -vṛt-/-vart-; not flagged. The reading of mātramahadvaṃ is uncertain; the list could also be read without 'dose'.

hindi: वहाँ पहले कही गई व्यापद् और उसका साधन।
english: There: the mishap as stated before, and its remedy (sādhana).
notes: Elliptical line with no verb. Read as vyāpat + sādhanam (two words); alternatively vyāpat-sādhanam as one compound 'mishap-remedy', with pūrvoktā agreeing with an unstated noun. Not resolved.

words.gloss: pleasant to the heart (first member of a compound continued in the next tokens)
scraping; vaṭaka (a small cake or pill)
words.gram: comp. members (ka stands in the next token)

hindi: इसके बाद भी वह ऊपर की ओर उठता है; हृद्य, अवलेखन और वटक को छोड़कर तीसरी औषध का प्रयोग न करे।
english: Even after this it rises upward; except for the hṛdya, avalekhana and vaṭaka (kinds), one should not apply a third medicine.

text_flags.why: possible: the words are wrongly divided in print (b for v, and ka separated from vaṭa); sense guessed as hṛdya-avalekhana-vaṭaka-varjam

notes: GLOSSARY OPEN: avacārayet rendered 'should apply' (plain literal). Subject of uttiṣṭhati is not stated. The reading of the compound is a guess from the damaged print; the meaning of hṛdya, avalekhana and vaṭaka as kinds of medicine is not stated in the line.

hindi: कठोर कोष्ठ वाले और अत्यन्त तीक्ष्ण अग्नि वाले में, अथवा अल्प वीर्य वाली औषध ऊपर की ओर जाने वाली हो या नीचे की ओर जाने वाली, भोजन के समान पाक को प्राप्त होती है।
english: In one with a hard bowel and very sharp fire (agni), or if the medicine is of little potency, whether directed to the upper part or to the lower part, it undergoes digestion like food.

text_flags.why: possible: agneḥ/agner damaged, with r displaced to the next token
possible: spelling, ūrdhva with long ū

notes: The grouping of the vā-alternatives is uncertain (hard bowel and sharp fire together, or each separately).

words.gram: m. nom. pl. pass. part. nir-√hṛ

hindi: वहाँ उभरे हुए दोष यथासमय बाहर न निकाले जाने पर विभ्रम उत्पन्न करते हैं।
english: There the aroused doṣas, if not expelled at the proper time, produce a disturbance (vibhrama).
notes: vibhrama: literally 'wandering about, confusion'; no specific condition is named in the line.

hindi: उस सुस्निग्ध कोष्ठ वाले को पर्याप्त अन्न और औषध पिलाए।
english: One should make him, whose bowel is well unctuous, drink a plentiful amount of food and the medicine.
notes: The line literally has 'food' and 'medicine' as objects of the causative 'drink'. GLOSSARY OPEN: pāyayet rendered literally 'should cause to drink'.

words.gloss: by one not oiled and not sweated

hindi: अल्प प्रत्यय वाला कषाय, या रूक्ष औषध, स्निग्ध और स्वेदित न किए हुए के द्वारा, अथवा शीत उपचार के साथ पिया जाए, तो वह स्तब्ध दोष वाला, गाँठ पड़ा हुआ अयोगि हो जाता है।
english: A decoction of little content (pratyaya), or a dry medicine, drunk by one not oiled and sweated, or with cold treatment, becomes ayogi, with the doṣas stiffened and clumped.

text_flags.why: typo: svinnema for the instrumental svinnena

notes: GLOSSARY: kaṣāya = decoction (OPEN, kept as decoction; it can also mean the astringent taste). alpapratyaya and ayogi are doubtful in sense: pratyaya may be 'ingredient, basis'; ayogi is rendered literally 'not duly joined'. The subject of bhavati is not stated.

words.gloss: him whose doṣas are much agitated

hindi: वहाँ वमन से फिर वमन कराए; स्निग्ध और स्वेदित किए हुए को विरेचन से फिर विरेचन कराए; अथवा जिसके बहुत दोष उभरे हुए हों उसे तीसरे दिन।
english: In that case one should make him vomit again with vomiting; one who has been oiled and sweated one should purge again with purging; or one whose doṣas are much agitated, on the third day.
notes: The clauses are elliptical; the division into three cases is the plainest reading. virecanam could also be 'the purgative'. 'Third day' is counted as stated, without further interpretation.

hindi: और दोनों संशोधनों में लवण और तैल से अभ्यक्त को पिण्ड और प्रस्तर से स्वेदित कराए।
english: And in both purifications, one anointed with salt and oil should be made to sweat by lump (piṇḍa) and layer (prastara).

text_flags.why: possible: should be one word by sandhi (tailābhyaktam); the space is a print error

notes: ubhayoḥ saṃśodhanayoḥ can be genitive ('of both') or locative ('in both'); 'in both' chosen. lavaṇataila is 'salt and oil' or 'salted oil'. piṇḍa and prastara are kept as literal words, not identified.

words.gloss: excessive heaviness and stiffness of the belly

hindi: स्निग्ध और स्वेदित किए हुए, वमन न कराकर विरेचन पीने वाले का, या आम सहित का, या मृदु विरेचन से विरिक्त का, नीचे के भाग में अत्यन्त भारीपन, पेट की कठोरता, शूल, तथा वात और मल का अवरोध होता है।
english: In one who was oiled and sweated, and who drank a purgative without having been made to vomit, or one with raw (āma) matter, or one mildly purged, there occur in the lower part excessive heaviness and stiffness of the belly, piercing pain, and obstruction of wind (vāta) and stool.
notes: The grouping of the genitives and of 'mṛdu vā' is the plainest reading; mṛdu may be read 'mildly' (with viriktasya) or as 'a mild (purgative)'. śūla is glossed 'piercing pain', not a named disease.

words.gloss: having set up, having given āsthāpana (literally 'making stand')
with juices of jāṅgala (of dry land)
prepared with phala, dāru and pippalī (drug names)

hindi: उस अयोगि को भी मूत्र सहित तीक्ष्ण द्रव्यों से आस्थापन करके, जाङ्गल रसों से भोजन कराकर, फल, दारु और पिप्पली से सिद्ध तैल से अनुवासन करके, वात को हरने वाले स्नेहों से फिर स्निग्ध करके, पुनः तीक्ष्ण द्रव्यों से विरेचन कराए।
english: Having given even him, the ayogin one, āsthāpana with sharp (substances) together with urine, having fed him with jāṅgala juices, having given anuvāsana with oil prepared with phala, dāru and pippalī, and having made him further unctuous with Vāta-taking-away oils, one should purge him again with sharp (substances).
notes: āsthāpana and anuvāsana are kept as the text's own words with a literal gloss; the line does not say what they are. 'Sharp (ones)' leaves the noun unstated, as in the Sanskrit. phala, dāru, pippalī are left as drug names without identification. GLOSSARY OPEN: bhojayitvā 'having fed', virecayet 'should purge'.

words.gloss: dullness, drowsiness, weakness, sinking of the limbs

hindi: कफ की अधिकता वाले, अत्यन्त स्निग्ध, भारी कोष्ठ वाले, या मन्द अग्नि वाले को मृदु रूप से दी गई औषध दोषों को अत्यन्त उभारकर जड़ता, तन्द्रा, दुर्बलता और अंगों की शिथिलता उत्पन्न करती है।
english: For one with Kapha abundant, very unctuous, heavy in the bowel, or of slow fire (agni), a medicine mildly administered, having greatly agitated the doṣas, produces dullness, drowsiness, weakness and sinking of the limbs.

text_flags.why: possible: m wrongly moved to the next token

notes: jāḍya is glossed plainly as 'dullness'; aṅgasāda as 'sinking of the limbs'. 'Of the bowel' (koṣṭhasya) with guru is read as a bahuvrīhi 'heavy-bowelled'.

hindi: उसे शीघ्र उल्लिखित करे।
english: One should scrape that up quickly.
notes: What 'tat' refers to, and what is scraped up, is not stated; ullikhet is kept literal ('scrape up').

hindi: उपवास कराए हुए और जिसकी अग्नि प्रदीप्त हो गई हो, फिर स्निग्ध किए हुए को तीक्ष्ण और उष्ण द्रव्यों से शुद्ध करे।
english: One who has been made to fast (laṅghana), whose fire (agni) has been kindled, and who has again been made unctuous, one should purify with sharp and hot (ones).
notes: 'Sharp and hot (ones)': noun not stated. laṅghita is kept literal ('made to fast', laṅghana).

words.gloss: for one with residue and bloating
for one having Vāta and phlegm

hindi: अवशेष और आध्मान वाले, वात और कफ वाले, रूक्ष, उदावर्त वाले, या मन्द अग्नि वाले को दी गई शीत अथवा रूक्ष औषध अत्यन्त आध्मान उत्पन्न करती है।
english: For one with residue and bloating, one with Vāta and phlegm, one dry, one with udāvarta (upward-turning), or one of slow fire (agni), a cold or dry medicine given produces great bloating (ādhmāna).

text_flags.why: possible: ādhmāna expected as in the same line; read as given, with ādhmāya for ādhmāna

notes: saśeṣādhmāya is uncertain: sa-śeṣa-ādhmāya 'with residue and bloating' is taken; 'saśeṣāya ādhmāya' is another division. Not resolved.

words.gloss: pricking in the anus and bladder

hindi: वहाँ मल के अवरोध से बँधकर पेट को जलाता है, और भीतर शूल, चमड़े की थैली के समान दोनों पार्श्वों में भरापन, सिर और पीठ में पीड़ा, श्वास, तथा गुदा और मूत्राशय में चुभन होती है।
english: There, from obstruction of waste, having bound up, it burns the belly, and there occur inner piercing pain, fullness of the two flanks like a leather bag, pain of the head and back, śvāsa (breath), and pricking in the anus and bladder.
notes: The subject of dahati is not stated. śvāsa is left as 'breath (śvāsa)' without naming a disease. basti is rendered 'bladder' here as a body part.

words.gloss: with the procedures of anointing, sweating, wick (varti), kindling, powder, and basti

hindi: उदावर्त और आनाह को हरने वाली अभ्यंग, स्वेद, वर्ति, दीपन, चूर्ण और बस्ति की क्रियाओं से उसका उपचार करे।
english: One should treat him with the procedures of anointing, sweating, wick (varti), kindling, powder and basti, which take away udāvarta and ānāha.

text_flags.why: possible: the word is wrongly divided in print

notes: The relative clause 'taking away udāvarta and ānāha' is taken to qualify the whole list of procedures. varti, dīpana, cūrṇa, basti are kept as literal words.

words.gloss: with soft bowel (koṣṭha) and soft fire (agni)

hindi: क्षाम, अल्प बल वाले, मृदु कोष्ठ और अग्नि वाले, रूक्ष, स्निग्ध, स्वेदित, अथवा आम सहित व्यक्ति द्वारा प्रयुक्त बलवान् औषध पित्त सहित वायु को दूषित करके परिकर्तिका उत्पन्न करती है।
english: When a strong medicine is taken by one who is lean, of little strength, with soft bowel and soft fire, dry, or oiled, sweated, or with raw (āma) matter, it corrupts wind (anila) together with Pitta and brings about parikartikā (cutting-around pain).
notes: Instrumentals are read as 'taken by'. kṣāma is glossed 'lean' (alternatives: emaciated, wasted). The grouping of rūkṣa/snigdha/svinna/sāma is the plainest reading.

words.gloss: in the navel, bladder, anus and male organ

hindi: वहाँ नाभि, मूत्राशय, गुदा और मेढ्र में दाह सहित काटने जैसी पीड़ा, वायु का अवरोध और विष्टम्भ होता है।
english: There: in the navel, bladder, anus and male organ, cutting-around pain with burning, obstruction of wind (anila), and binding.
notes: No verb is stated; 'occur' is not added. viṣṭambha is kept literal ('binding, obstruction').

words.gloss: joined with black tila, madhuka and honey (madhu)

hindi: उसे काले तिल, मधुक और मधु से युक्त पिच्छा-बस्तियों से आस्थापन करे।
english: One should give him āsthāpana with picchā-bastis joined with black tila, madhuka and honey.
notes: tila and madhuka are kept as drug names without identification; 'black' is taken with tila. picchā ('slime, sliminess') is kept literal. 'Joined with' could govern only the last items; the plainest reading is taken.

words.gloss: with milk boiled with the milk-bearing trees (kṣīrivṛkṣa)

hindi: अथवा क्षीरिवृक्षों के साथ पकाए हुए दूध से।
english: Or with milk boiled with the milk-bearing trees (kṣīrivṛkṣa).
notes: Elliptical: continues the previous unit (no verb). The phrase kṣīrivṛkṣa is rendered by its literal sense, not identified.

words.gloss: with ghee-maṇḍa (the clear upper part of ghee)

hindi: और इसे शीतल जल से सींचकर, जिसने दूध के साथ भोजन किया हो, उसे घृतमण्ड और यष्टीमधुक के तैल से अनुवासन करे।
english: And one should give him, sprinkled with cold water and having eaten with milk, anuvāsana with ghee-maṇḍa and with oil of yaṣṭīmadhuka.
notes: payasā bhuktavantam is read 'having eaten with milk'. ghṛtamaṇḍena and the yaṣṭīmadhuka oil are taken as two means ('and'), not as one; the Sanskrit has no 'and'. yaṣṭīmadhuka is kept as a drug name.

hindi: क्षाम के लिए मधुर और बृंहण, सब विधि इष्ट है।
english: For one who is lean, every procedure that is sweet and bulking is desired.
notes: bṛṃhaṇa is rendered 'bulking' (literally 'making grow'). The words 'sweet and bulking' are taken together as qualifying vidhi.

hindi: आम सहित में लंघन और दीपन, और हल्का, रूक्ष और उष्ण अन्न-पान।
english: In one with raw (āma) matter: fasting (laṅghana) and kindling (dīpana), and food and drink that is light, dry and hot.
notes: No verb is stated; the line is elliptical and continues the previous unit.

words.gloss: when become free of raw (āma) matter

hindi: आम से रहित हो जाने पर (मध्यम बल के उपचारों के समान, वायु और धूप के समान, धूल और भस्म के बिखेरने से इत्यादि) वात के अनुरोध से भोजन और पान में हल्का, क्षारयुक्त और खट्टा प्रयुक्त करे; वात के अधिक होने पर खटाई सहित दही, दाडिम की त्वचा से युक्त, भोजन और पान में प्रयुक्त करे।
english: When one has become free of raw (āma) matter (as with treatments of middle strength, as by wind and sun, by scattering dust and ash, and so on), in accordance with Vāta one should employ in food and drink what is light, alkaline and sour; when Vāta is in excess, curd with sour added, joined with the skin of dāḍima.

text_flags.why: possible: instrumental plural expected; r lost
possible: anurodha expected; 'anuraṃdha' is not a known word

notes: The bracketed words look like an inserted note in the edition (the brackets are in the printed text); kept and translated. The two printed parts after 'vāte' are read as a locative absolute 'when Vāta is in excess'. The sentence is hard: the reading is tentative.

hindi: और दाडिम के रस सहित घृत पिए।
english: And one should drink ghee (sarpis) together with dāḍima juice.
notes: The 'ca' stands after sadāḍimarasaṃ in the printed order; the plainest reading is taken.

words.gloss: paste of tila and devadāru (drug names)

hindi: अथवा उष्ण जल से तिल और देवदारु का कल्क।
english: Or, with hot water, a paste (kalka) of tila and devadāru.
notes: Elliptical (no verb); tila and devadāru are drug names, not identified.

words.gloss: of one with a hard bowel (koṣṭha)

words.gram: n. nom. sg. p.p. caus. ava-√car

hindi: कठोर कोष्ठ वाले और बहुत दोष वाले में अल्प मात्रा और अल्प गुण वाला, मृदु या स्निग्ध, प्रयुक्त शोधन औषध दोषों को उभारकर बाहर नहीं निकालती; और थोड़ा-थोड़ा पित्त और कफ से मिला हुआ बह निकलता है।
english: In one with a hard bowel and many doṣas, a purifying medicine applied, of small dose and quality, mild or unctuous, having agitated the doṣas does not expel them; and, little by little, mixed with Pitta and Kapha, it flows out all round.

text_flags.why: possible: y for p; 'little by little' fits

notes: The subject of parisravati is not stated (the doṣas or the medicine). 'alpamātraguṇam' could also be read 'of small dose, without quality'. GLOSSARY: kvātha/kaṣāya not involved.

words.gloss: binding, heaviness, drying (śoṣa), koṭha (term kept), itching, paleness, sinking of the limbs, piercing pain

hindi: और विष्टम्भ, भारीपन, शोष, कोठ, खुजली, पाण्डुता, अंगों की शिथिलता और शूल उत्पन्न करता है।
english: And it brings about binding, heaviness, drying (śoṣa), koṭha, itching, paleness, sinking of the limbs and piercing pain.
notes: The subject (the medicine or the retained doṣas) is not stated. koṭha is a technical word and is kept untranslated.

words.gloss: with decoctions of tiniśa, dhava, aśvakarṇa, palāśa and valā (drug names)

hindi: उसे तिनिश, धव, अश्वकर्ण, पलाश और बला के निर्यूहों से, मधु मिलाकर, आस्थापन करे।
english: One should give him āsthāpana with decoctions (niryūha) of tiniśa, dhava, aśvakarṇa, palāśa and valā, joined with honey.
notes: GLOSSARY OPEN: niryūha is rendered 'decoction', the same as kaṣāya and kvātha so far. The five names are drug names, not identified.

hindi: और जिसका परिस्रव शान्त हो गया हो, उसे फिर और स्निग्ध करके तीक्ष्ण द्रव्यों से शुद्ध करे।
english: And one whose flowing out has subsided, having again been made further unctuous, one should purify with sharp (ones).
notes: The noun for 'sharp (ones)' is not stated.

words.gloss: kindling (ones) (split across two tokens in print)
āsavas, ariṣṭas and so on (names of prepared drinks)

hindi: और शुद्ध हो जाने पर दीपन चूर्णों तथा आसव, अरिष्ट आदि का प्रयोग करे।
english: And when purified, one should employ kindling (dīpana) ones: powders, āsavas, ariṣṭas and so on.

text_flags.why: possible: dīpanān is wrongly divided in print, and the ā of āsava is lost

notes: Whether dīpanān qualifies only the powders or also the āsavas and ariṣṭas is not clear. āsava and ariṣṭa are kept as the text's own words.
